opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin only if role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code). Requested level equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: IT database confirms role: Payroll Specialist. Full-time employee; role does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer), so maximum is write. Requested write equals maximum, recommend write.
Note 3 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Finance database confirms role: Payroll Specialist. Full-time employee. Source Code is owned by Engineer; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code, so maximum is write for full-time employees. Requested write equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 4 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Compliance database confirms role: Payroll Specialist. Employment type full_time per HR/Finance records. Source Code is owned by Engineer; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code, so maximum for a full-time employee is write. Requested write equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities database confirms role: Payroll Specialist (same as HR/IT/Finance/Compliance). Employee is full-time per HR records. Source Code is owned by Engineer; Payroll Specialist does not own it, so maximum for full-time employee is write. Requested write equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security database shows E042 is a contractor with basic security training, differing from HR's full_time note. Contractors max is read unless they have advanced training; with basic training, max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about Edward Fleming (E042). HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, and Facilities report full_time (max write for Source Code, since Payroll Specialist does not own the system), while the Security database reports contractor with basic security training (max read for contractors without advanced training). Given the direct conflict and the policy that contractors with only basic training may not exceed read, I apply the more restrictive interpretation to avoid granting access above the permitted maximum. Requested write exceeds that maximum, so grant read.
